stem.text: The nth partial sum of the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \) is \( S_n = \frac{9 n^{2} - 7}{4 n + 6} \) for \( n \ge 1 \). Does the series converge? If it does, find its sum.

answer_key.label: The series diverges, because its partial sums grow without bound.

worked_solution.text: A series converges exactly when its sequence of partial sums approaches a finite limit.
worked_solution.rule_named: convergence as the limit of the partial sums

worked_solution.text: The numerator has degree 2 and the denominator degree 1, so \( S_n \to \infty \). The series diverges, even though its terms \( a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} \) approach \( \frac{9}{4} \).

options.label: The series converges, and its sum is \( \frac{9}{4} \).
options.derivation: the limit of the terms reported as the sum of the series
